status: IMPLEMENTED, INTEGRATED and VERIFIED: native World-loss client drain and registration gating; overall mission active
contract: Native listener drops new sockets before a valid current-connection registration ACK; CONNECT handler separately requires IsRegistered.

ACK body parses BYTE nation, WORD operators + DWORD IDs, WORD message pairs + bounded length-prefixed strings, exactly to end. Unexpected pre-registration opcode, malformed body or five-second timeout closes connection.

Detected read/write/framing failure or escaping handler exception clears admission, closes original socket, then awaits native client teardown before replacement dial. No replay of old queued writes to the new socket.

Native teardown closes all client sockets, awaits existing connection coroutines and pending background DB work. Ready-commit race follows the normal phase transition and final save even on closed sockets.

Successful final save atomically releases account with logout receipt; failed writes retain in-memory snapshot/generation and durable ready claim/current user. Unrelated accounts may reconnect; failed account cannot replace old generation.
Map ownership token and dedicated PostgreSQL connection survive World restart; no checkpoint recovery or synthetic source change is used for successful live-Map drain.
Map outbound composed writes serialize with one permit held through completion; original socket captured before waiting. Runtime lifecycle remains single-I/O-thread confined.
Surviving Map process and reconnect after draining is a modern policy; original World loss requested Map service shutdown. Client packet opcodes/fields unchanged.
